findings.title: Authorization negation defect: trailing negation and interrogative suppression leaked operations
findings.rationale: SPLIT, and the split is the disposition. The AUTHORIZATION path named in the title does not leak in this tree: probing the shipped module (src/scripts/git_authorization_hook.ts) with the three trailing/interrogative forms returns classifyAuthorization={"authorized":[],"evidence":{}} for "Merge PR #12 auf keinen Fall.", "Merge #12 under no circumstances." and "Merge PR #12? Actually, don't." — the 14.15.0 predecessor 13713a1a9ae6 closed that half in 6a08ed26, whose own rationale already names both shapes this finding reports. What IS live is the REVOCATION path, which the first fix never reached: isRevocation returns false for all three forms, and foldGrants (:704-712) drops grants only under isRevocation, so a prior standing grant survives an unambiguous withdrawal — measured foldGrants([{targets:[12],consumed:[]}], "Merge PR #12 auf keinen Fall.", [], ...) -> [[12]] SURVIVES, while "do not merge PR #12" -> [] correctly drops. Two negation grammars exist about 240 lines apart (NEGATION_WORD :750, 14 forms, clause-scoped both directions; REVOKE_RE :676, 10 forms, before-only, fixed 30-char window). NOT fixed: nothing has landed for the revocation path. NOT false_positive: the grant-survival is reproduced above. Carried as accepted_risk with a named receiver: agents/roadmaps/road-to-one-negation-vocabulary.md owns the consolidation of the two vocabularies into one clause-scoped implementation.
findings.verified_by: Independent reproduction 2026-09-04 against the shipped module at b75d7f7cb via npx tsx (isRevocation/classifyAuthorization over the three forms, plus a foldGrants grant-survival probe); code read of foldGrants src/scripts/git_authorization_hook.ts:704-712. Receiver roadmap: agents/roadmaps/road-to-one-negation-vocabulary.md. Predecessor comparison: 13713a1a9ae6 in agents/evidence/release-findings/14.15.0.json.

findings.title: Target extraction: 7-digit regex cap failed silently on 8-digit PR numbers
findings.rationale: REPEAT CLASS — a DUPLICATE REPORT of 14.15.0 finding 220223cedd5e, not a regression and not an uncovered instance. Checked against the tree, not the title: src/scripts/git_authorization_hook.ts:638 exports PR_NUMBER_MAX = 2147483647 and :656 matches (\d{1,10}), so the seven-digit cap the finding names is absent from the reviewed head. Why it was reported anyway is itself evidence for the documented-versus-introduced class recorded in Phase 2b of road-to-the-unwritten-ledger: the fix commit landed INSIDE the reviewed 14.15.0..14.16.0 span, and it left an explanatory comment at :644 that literally quotes the string 'The old `\d{1,7}` was' — so the only occurrence of the defect pattern in the diff is the fix's own description of what it removed. The 14.15.0 ledger, itself added inside the same span by 4d44188af, describes the defect again in prose.

findings.title: Closed-vocabulary property unpinned: patch text could reach refusal via future edit
findings.rationale: FALSE POSITIVE as a defect, and the gap it did identify is now closed. No leak path existed: describeImpact (src/scripts/hooks/merge_impact.ts:253-275) interpolates only pr, impact.filesChanged, impact.reason and impact.markers.join("; "), and every marker classifyDiff can push (:150-163) is either a literal from the DESTRUCTIVE_MARKERS table (:55-68), the literal at :157, or the MAJOR_BUMP string at :162 whose two interpolations are (\d+) captures (:136) — digits only. So patch text could not reach the refusal. What the finding correctly identified is that this property was asserted in comments and by no test; that pin now exists and is scoped over the classifyDiff -> describeImpact pipeline rather than describeImpact alone, which matters because markers is a caller-supplied string[]. Honest caveat: the literal-table assertion runs over a patch with no version bump, so the MAJOR_BUMP marker string is covered by the regex read rather than by that test.
findings.verified_by: tests/scripts/merge_impact_closed_vocabulary.test.ts:93 'every destructive marker label is a literal from the closed table', :109 'the only variable parts of the message are numbers', plus the sensitivity pair :124 'a message built by interpolating the diff is caught' and :136 'and it is not vacuous'. Run 2026-09-04: passed.

findings.title: security-sensitive-stop: five triggers added, two narrowed from obvious single word
findings.rationale: The finding describes the fix, not a defect. Both halves are literally accurate — bb857f113ca0fa9b4c621478412891d94dd1cad7 adds exactly five keywords (src/rules/security-sensitive-stop.md:15-19: file upload, ssrf, api resource, public endpoint, status endpoint) on top of six pre-existing ones at :9-14, and two are multi-word rather than the obvious single word. The narrowing is DELIBERATE with the rationale recorded in that commit message: keyword matching is word-boundary substring, so a bare 'upload' fires on "upload the roadmap" and a bare 'endpoint' fires on documentation edits; the bare form was the first implementation and was narrowed after an AI-council round named "Document the API endpoint parameter" as a real near-miss the rule's own section When NOT to fire excludes. That is the over-broad-single-word anti-pattern being avoided on purpose. Reported as style; adjudicated as intended design.
findings.verified_by: tests/eval/routing-matrix/security-sensitive-stop.yaml carries the four new positives AND four matching near-misses (including "Upload the roadmap to the shared drive." and "Document the API endpoint parameter in the reference page."), so the denial side is pinned, not only the claim side. Run via tests/scripts/routing_matrix.test.ts 2026-09-04: 193 passed.
